{{Quote|I mean, everyone thought you died on Anchoron.''"<br />"''In a very real sense, I did. The Emperor wasn’t quite able to kill me at Anchoron, but he might just as well have done so. He took everything I had except my life: my family, my profession, even all future contacts with mainstream Corellian society. He forced me outside the law I’d worked so hard to create and maintain. Forced me to become a rebel.|Han Solo and Garm Bel Iblis, in 9 ABY|<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>}}
The '''bombing of the Treitamma Political Center''' was committed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] under the direction of [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]] for the purpose of [[Assassin/Legends|assassinating]] [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]]. The senator's [[Bel Iblis family|family]] were [[Death/Legends|killed]], but Bel Iblis was outside the building at the [[Time/Legends|time]].

==Prelude==
[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] was suspicious of the dealings of<ref name="EGTC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> during the waning years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Suspecting that Palpatine was a force for evil, the charismatic senator worked to undermine his support in the Senate with some successes.<ref name="LC sourcebook">''[[The Last Command Sourcebook]]''</ref> However, Bel Iblis's actions caused him to lose influence,<ref name="EGTC" /> and Palpatine declared himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEC" />

The [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] senator did not hide his disdain for the Emperor and continued working discretely to undermine the Empire.<ref name="TFU Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Palpatine later decided to have Bel Iblis killed.<ref name="Dark Force Rising" /> By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="Readers" /> At the direction of [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]], a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] was planted at the [[Treitamma Political Center]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Anchoron]], where Bel Iblis was due to give a speech. The senator travelled to the world with his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Arrianya Bel Iblis]] and<ref name="Interlude" /> their two [[Arrianya and Garm Bel Iblis's daughters|daughters]].<ref name="AoR Core" /> Tensions between the two parents had grown in the preceeding [[Standard month/Legends|months]] due to Arrianya's staunchly pro-Imperial values and faith in the Emperor.<ref name="Interlude" />

==The bombing==
Garm Bel Iblis happened to be outside of the political center to meet with "[[Aach]]," an agent of fellow senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]]. The explosion killed dozens or hundreds, including Arrianya and both of her<ref name="Interlude" /> and Garm's daughters.<ref name="AoR Core" />

==Aftermath==
Bel Iblis felt that the Emperor had taken everything from him and driven him to become a rebel.<ref name="Dark Force Rising" /> Following the loss of his family, the politically maverick senator became more withdrawn, sullen, and thoughtful.<ref name="LC sourcebook" /> His [[Aide/Legends|aide]] [[Sena Leikvold Midanyl]] helped Bel Iblis overcome his grief.<ref name="Sena databank">{{DB|character|sena|Midanyl, Sena Leikvold}}</ref> The majority in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] believed Bel Iblis to have been killed,<ref name="Rebellion Era" /> which Palpatine did not deny to intimidate his opponents.<ref name="TFU Campaign Guide" /> Many Corellians mourned his loss.<ref name="AoR Core" /> The senator also founded the [[Corellian Resistance/Legends|Corellian Resistance]] using his own [[Currency/Legends|finances]].<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> He continued seeking assistance from Mothma and Organa,<ref name="TFU Campaign Guide" /> and, like the former, worked to recruit others to the Rebel cause.<ref name="Rebellion Era">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

In [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]],<ref name="Thrawn Trilogy date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places the events of the [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|Thrawn trilogy]], which includes [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] meeting with [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]].</ref> the Corellian Rebel [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] met Bel Iblis and was surprised to find that he had survived<ref name="Dark Force Rising" /> the bombing.<ref name="Interlude" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Empire's attempt to kill Garm Bel Iblis on Anchoron was first mentioned in the [[1992]] [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|Thrawn trilogy]] novel ''[[Dark Force Rising]]'', written by [[Timothy Zahn]].<ref name="Dark Force Rising" /> It made its first appearance in Part 1 of the short story "[[Interlude at Darkknell]]," also written by Zahn and published in [[1999]] in the anthology ''[[Tales from the New Republic]]''.<ref name="Interlude" /> The explosion was first identified in Armand Isard's entry in [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE Armand">{{CSWECite|II|117|Isard, Armand}}</ref>

The [[2012]] ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] dates the events of "Interlude at Darkknell" to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], but acknowledges that its events are difficult to place, as the narrative portrays Bel Iblis learning about the Death Star, which he had already seen in person as portrayed<ref name="Readers">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> in the 2008 [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> Other aspects in the short story, such as the age of [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]], indicate that the story takes place in 0 BBY.<ref name="Readers" /> The [[2009]] ''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''<ref name="Rebellion Era" /> and the [[2014]] [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]] placed the bombing that killed Bel Iblis's family prior to the signing of the Corellian Treaty in 2 BBY.<ref name="AoR Core" /> 

The ''[[The Last Command Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Eric S. Trautmann]] and published in [[1994]], referred to Bel Iblis's presumed death on Anchoron but stated that his family was instead killed shortly after the [[Declaration of a New Order|establishment]] of the Empire<ref name="LC sourcebook" /> which took place in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Bel Iblis's opposition to Palpatine led him to direct his anger towards the Corellian senator, and, shortly after declaring himself Emperor, having Bel Iblis and his family captured<ref name="LC sourcebook" /> by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Garm was forced to watch his wife and children be executed, although he managed to escape. Later, he refused to explain how he did so.<ref name="LC sourcebook" /> ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', written by [[Andy Mangels]] and published in [[1995]], stated that the arrest of Bel Iblis's family took place on Anchoron.<ref name="EGTC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Bel Iblis's entry in the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]],<ref name="Databank">{{DB|character|garmbeliblis|Bel Iblis, Garm}}</ref> which was reprinted in ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'', stated that the Empire executed his family while forcing Garm to watch.<ref name="CSWE Garm">{{CSWECite|Bel Iblis, Garm|I|68}}</ref>
